questions.q: Which building is considered Leandro Locsin's 'Magnum Opus,' famously described as a 'floating' block of travertine marble held up by curved concrete buttresses?
o: The Manila Hotel
The National Museum of Fine Arts
The Cultural Center of the Philippines (Main Theater)
The Philippine International Convention Center (PICC)
questions.n: Completed in 1969, the CCP is the definitive example of Locsin's 'floating volume' concept.

questions.q: The Church of the Holy Sacrifice in UP Diliman was Locsin's first major project. What makes its structure unique in Philippine history?
o: It was the first circular church with a thin-shell concrete dome in the country
It was the first building made of glass
It was built entirely underground
It was the first church to use gold leaf on the exterior
questions.n: This 1955 structure was revolutionary for its time, featuring a column-free interior and a dome only a few inches thick.

questions.q: Locsin designed the 'Istana Nurul Iman,' which holds the Guinness World Record for being the world's largest residential palace. In which country is it located?
o: Brunei
Malaysia
The Philippines
Saudi Arabia
questions.n: Locsin was commissioned by the Sultan of Brunei to design this massive palace, blending modern engineering with Islamic architectural motifs.

questions.q: Many of Locsin's buildings, like the PICC and the CCP, are associated with 'Brutalism.' What does this term imply about the materials used?
o: The buildings are designed to look 'brutal' or scary
The extensive use of raw, exposed concrete (béton brut)
The use of recycled materials from war zones
Buildings that have no windows
questions.n: Locsin loved the plasticity and strength of concrete, often leaving the texture of the wooden formworks visible on the surface.

questions.q: Locsin's design for the 'Philippine Pavilion' at the 1970 World Expo in Osaka, Japan, was famous for its shape. What did it resemble?
o: A Spanish Galleon
A giant bamboo shoot
An erupting volcano
A stylized, soaring nipa hut (Bahay Kubo) silhouette
questions.n: Locsin often reinterpreted the steep roof of the Bahay Kubo into dramatic, modern concrete forms.

questions.q: The Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) is a complex of four modular buildings. Which specific feature is a recurring Locsin signature found in its grand lobby?
o: Intricate Spanish-style wood carvings
A massive cantilevered staircase and a 'floating' ceiling
Walls made entirely of adobe and thatch
Tall, slender Ionic columns
questions.n: Locsin often designed staircases and ceilings that appear to be suspended in mid-air, emphasizing the 'Poet of Space' title.

questions.q: Which Locsin-designed building in Makati features a prominent 'L-shaped' plan and was once the tallest building in the Philippines upon its completion in 1968?
o: The Ayala Museum (Original Building)
The Peninsula Manila
The LV Locsin Building
The SSS Building
questions.n: This building served as his own firm's headquarters and represents his mature style of interlocking concrete volumes.

questions.q: Locsin's design for the Monastery of the Transfiguration in Malaybalay, Bukidnon, is famous for its roof. What shape does it take?
o: A giant pyramid
A perfect sphere
A series of pointed Gothic spires
A flat, industrial warehouse roof
questions.n: The heavy, black-shingled pyramidal roof evokes the silhouette of a traditional hut while feeling grounded in the mountain landscape.

questions.q: In the design of the CCP Main Theater, Locsin used 'Travertine' for the exterior. What is the visual effect of this material?
o: It turns the building bright red in the sunlight
It makes the building look like a shiny glass mirror
It makes the building transparent at night
It provides a warm, textured stone finish that softens the massive concrete forms
questions.n: Locsin used this imported stone to add a sense of luxury and timelessness to the Brutalist concrete structure.

questions.q: Leandro Locsin often emphasized the use of 'Passive Cooling' in his designs. How is this achieved in his residential works?
o: By installing the largest air conditioning units available
Painting all the walls black to absorb heat
Using wide eaves and open floor plans for natural cross-ventilation
Sealing all windows to keep the cold air inside
questions.n: By borrowing from the 'Bahay na Bato' and 'Bahay Kubo,' he allowed air to move freely through the house.

questions.q: Which bank headquarters in Makati is famous for its heavy, fortress-like concrete exterior designed by Locsin?
o: The BDO Corporate Center
The Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP)
The Philippine National Bank (PNB) Financial Center
The RCBC Plaza
questions.n: The LBP building is a clear example of Locsin's Brutalist style, featuring deep recessed windows and a powerful concrete facade.

questions.q: Locsin designed the 'St. Andrew the Apostle Church' in Makati. What is the unique floor plan of this building?
o: A standard rectangular basilica
A giant cross shape when viewed from above
An L-shape to fit the street corner
A circular plan exactly like the UP Church
questions.n: The church features a distinctive butterfly or tent-like shape with a cross-shaped plan that emphasizes a central gathering.

questions.q: True or False: Leandro Locsin was a talented pianist before he chose to pursue architecture full-time.
o: True
False
questions.n: His musical background is often cited as the reason for the 'rhythmic' and 'melodic' quality of his architectural spaces.

questions.q: Locsin's 'Benguet Center' in Mandaluyong was designed to resemble which Philippine cultural landmark?
o: Corregidor Island
The Chocolate Hills
Mayon Volcano
The Banaue Rice Terraces
questions.n: The building uses staggered, cantilevered floors to mimic the stepped look of the Cordillera terraces.

questions.q: What is the common nickname given to the CCP Main Building due to its heavy, dark opening beneath the floating block?
o: The Pillar
The Mouth
The Eye
The Cave
questions.n: The deep, recessed entrance is sometimes visually compared to a mouth that 'swallows' the audience into the world of theater.

questions.q: Locsin's design for the 'St. Andrew the Apostle Church' in Makati is famously topped with a massive 'crown' that doubles as what functional architectural element?
o: A water catchment tank
An observation deck for tourists
A giant air-conditioning vent
A stylized bell tower and skylight
questions.n: The dramatic white peaks atop the church serve to house the bells and draw light into the center of the cross-shaped floor plan.

questions.q: Which of these luxury hotels in Makati features a iconic 'fan-shaped' lobby and grand fountain designed by Leandro Locsin?
o: Fairmont Makati
The Peninsula Manila
The Manila Hotel
Makati Shangri-La
questions.n: Locsin designed the original structure, known for its sprawling, welcoming lobby that became a 'national living room' for Makati.

questions.q: Locsin designed the 'National Arts Center' in Los Baños. Which specific element of the site planning reflects his 'Poet of Space' philosophy?
o: The use of underground bunkers for rehearsals
The construction of a giant concrete wall to block the wind
The placement of a giant glass pyramid in the forest
The terraced layout that follows the natural contours of Mt. Makiling
questions.n: He integrated the buildings into the mountain, ensuring that the architecture felt like a natural extension of the landscape.

questions.q: In his design for the 'Philippine Stock Exchange Plaza' (Ayala Triangle), Locsin utilized a 'curtain wall.' How does this differ from his usual Brutalist style?
o: It uses heavy adobe stones instead of concrete
It features hand-painted murals on the exterior
It emphasizes transparency and light through glass and aluminum rather than massive concrete
It is built entirely out of bamboo
questions.n: This project showed Locsin's versatility in using 'slick' modern materials while still maintaining his signature sense of scale.

questions.q: The 'Manila International Airport' (now NAIA Terminal 1) was another Locsin project. What was the primary structural challenge he solved in its design?
o: Designing a wide-span, column-free passenger terminal using massive concrete beams
Making the roof look like an airplane wing
Creating a building that could float on water
Building a terminal that was completely invisible from the air
questions.n: He used his expertise in concrete to create a grand, open interior space that could handle massive crowds without structural clutter.

questions.q: Locsin's 'PLDT Tower' in Makati is noted for its 'sun-shading' fins. What is the practical purpose of these vertical concrete elements?
o: To reduce solar heat gain while allowing natural light to enter
To provide a place for birds to nest
To act as lightning rods
To reinforce the building against giant waves
questions.n: In a tropical climate, these 'brise-soleil' elements are essential for energy efficiency and occupant comfort.

questions.q: True or False: Leandro Locsin designed the original 'Ayala Museum,' which was later demolished to make way for the current glass structure.
o: True
False
questions.n: The original 1974 building was a masterpiece of Brutalist geometry that showcased his ability to design intimate cultural spaces.

questions.q: Which of these materials did Locsin often use for the INTERIORS of his buildings to provide a 'Filipino' warmth to the cold concrete?
o: Recycled rubber tires
Native hardwoods like Narra and Capiz shells
Industrial stainless steel
Imported Greek plastic
questions.n: He masterfully integrated traditional Filipino materials into modern settings to create a unique 'Tropical Modernist' interior.

questions.q: Locsin's 'Folk Arts Theater' (Tanghalang Balagtas) was built in a record-breaking 77 days. What structural system allowed for such speed?
o: A space-frame roof and pre-cast concrete panels
It was 3D printed
It was made of inflatable fabric
A simple wooden frame
questions.n: The use of pre-engineered and prefabricated components allowed the team to assemble the massive structure in just weeks.

questions.q: In the 'Church of the Holy Sacrifice,' the altar is placed in the center. What was the liturgical significance of this choice?
o: To emphasize the community gathered around the Eucharist (Mass)
To provide more space for a giant organ
To save money on building walls
To make it easier for the priest to leave early
questions.n: This 'Church in the Round' concept was a radical move toward more inclusive and participatory religious ceremonies.
